key_insight: A simple atom-selection strategy called "deletions" more reliably extracts local atomic environments from large simulations for DFT training than more elaborate methods.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate and efficient generation of reference data for machine-learning interatomic potentials in large-scale molecular dynamics and active-learning workflows.
method: Benchmark multiple extraction approaches for embedding local environments into smaller periodic DFT cells
Test across diverse systems: amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C
Compare geometry choices and passivation needs for the extracted atom sets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark study across several material systems and states that deletions consistently outperformed alternative extraction methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the extracted cluster and any passivating envelope preserve the local chemistry at the chosen boundary.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
